nodes.title: Bounds for the arithmetic derivative

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be the arithmetic derivative and $C$ the accelerated Collatz map. For a prime $p$, $D(C(p^p)) = C(D(p^p))$ if and only if $C(p^p) = q^q$ for some prime $q$.
nodes.title: Prime tetrations where the arithmetic derivative and the Collatz map commute

nodes.summary: Suppose the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are compatible, where $q < p$. Then $r \ge 241$, $s \ge 241$, $3q < r < 3p$ and $3q < s < 3p$.
nodes.title: Bounds on the factors of compatible semiprimes

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be the arithmetic derivative and $C$ the accelerated Collatz map. Let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $t \ge 0$ be an integer with $t^2 = p^2 - 22pq + q^2 - 8$. If $r = (p + q + t)/4$ and $s = (p + q - t)/4$ are both primes, then $C(pq) = rs$ and $D(C(pq)) = C(D(pq))$.
nodes.title: Prime roots give semiprime solutions

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be the accelerated Collatz map and $T$ the Collatz map. For every even natural number $n$, $C(n) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: The accelerated Collatz map on even numbers

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be the accelerated Collatz map and $T$ the Collatz map. For every odd natural number $n$, $C(n) = T(T(n))$.
nodes.title: The accelerated Collatz map on odd numbers

nodes.summary: The accelerated Collatz map $C : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sends a natural number $n$ to $n/2$ if $n$ is even and to $(3n + 1)/2$ if $n$ is odd.
nodes.title: The accelerated Collatz map

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be the arithmetic derivative and $C$ the accelerated Collatz map. Every positive integer $n$ with $D(C(n)) = C(D(n))$ is composite, that is, $n > 1$ and $n$ is not prime.
nodes.title: Positive solutions of the Collatz arithmetic differential equation are composite
An example of compatible semiprimes

nodes.summary: Natural numbers $p, q, r, s$ form a compatible semiprime pair, and the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are called compatible, when $p, q, r, s$ are primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$; equivalently, $r$ and $s$ are the roots of $2x^2 - (p + q)x + 3pq + 1 = 0$.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r, s$ be primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$, so that the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are compatible. Then one of $p, q$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $4$ modulo $5$, and likewise one of $r, s$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $4$ modulo $5$.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes modulo 5

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r, s$ be primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$, so that the semiprime $pq$ is compatible with the semiprime $rs$. Then $pq \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and one of $p, q$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $3$ modulo $4$.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes modulo 4

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r, s$ be primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$, so that the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are compatible. Then one of $p, q$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $9$ modulo $10$, and likewise one of $r, s$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $9$ modulo $10$.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes modulo 10

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r, s$ be primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$, so that the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are compatible. Then $pq \equiv rs \equiv 2 \pmod 3$; moreover one of $p, q$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $2$ modulo $3$, and likewise one of $r, s$ is congruent to $1$ and the other to $2$ modulo $3$.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes modulo 3

nodes.title: No special semiprime solves the derivative–Collatz equation

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be the arithmetic derivative and $C$ the accelerated Collatz map. Every positive integer $n$ with $D(C(n)) = C(D(n))$ is odd.
nodes.title: Positive solutions of the Collatz arithmetic differential equation are odd

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r, s$ be primes with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$, so that the semiprimes $pq$ and $rs$ are compatible. Then $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ are all odd.
nodes.title: Compatible semiprimes have odd prime factors

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be the arithmetic derivative and let $C$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $C(n) = n/2$ for even $n$ and $C(n) = (3n + 1)/2$ for odd $n$. If $p$ and $q$ are primes with $q < p$ and $D(C(pq)) = C(D(pq))$, then $p - q \ge 2\sqrt{30p^2 + 2} - 10p$.
nodes.title: Prime gap bound for semiprime solutions

nodes.summary: Call a natural number $n$ a compatible semiprime if $n = pq$ for primes $p, q$ for which there are primes $r, s$ with $2(r + s) = p + q$ and $2rs = 3pq + 1$. The sum of $1/n$ over all compatible semiprimes $n$ converges.
nodes.title: Reciprocals of compatible semiprimes have a finite sum
